To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of gene classification and position-frequency matrix-based prediction of individual and pairs of binding sites in the promoters of function-specific genes can be used to predict the transcription factors regulating gene expression in specific biological paradigms.
the proximal promoter regions of function-specific genes contain a significant number of transcription-factor binding site motifs, which can be predicted with high accuracy.
we developed a methodology to predict function-specific transcription-factor binding sites with high specificity and sensitivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the prediction of function-specific transcription-factor binding sites and with the analysis of the regulatory network of transcription factors and their binding sites in proximally located promoters of human genes.
the development of a computational framework to identify function-specific transcription-factor binding sites.
the development of a new computational approach for the identification of transcription-factor binding-site motifs in the proximal promoter of human genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methodology described in this paper can be used for accurate prediction of transcription-factor binding site and for the detection of cooperation between transcription factors.
the presented approach provides a powerful and robust tool for the detection and annotation of transcription factor binding sites in the genome.
our approach is able to detect transcription-factor binding sites with high sensitivity and specificity in function-specific proximal promoters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proximal promoter region of human genes is rich in binding motifs of transcription factors.
we developed a new methodology to accurately predict transcription-factor binding sites and validated the results by microarray transcript profiling and literature-derived protein interactions.
we have identified the transcription-factor binding-site motifs that are overrepresented in the proximal promoter regions of genes involved in specific biological processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to predict transcription-factor binding sites and their cooperation in the proximal promoter of function-specific genes with a reasonable degree of accuracy.
the combination of gene classification, genome sequence data, and position-frequency matrices of transcription factors can significantly increase the accuracy of binding site detection.

the use of Gene Ontology biological processes as a priori information for transcription-factor binding site prediction increases accuracy of the prediction and helps to identify function-specific transcription factors.
